title: Registry document
description: The one JSON object at registry/registry.json. The gateway accepts or rejects it whole. Source: docs/plan/02-contracts.md -> Registry document, and ADR-0002. Freezes at G1a, except $defs/oauth, which freezes at G1b.

schemaVersion.description: The version of this contract. 1 is a document whose entries carry no fragments, and keeps the meaning it had before fragments existed; 2 is a document whose entries may carry them, and one whose entries carry any must declare 2 (the if/then below). A build accepts exactly the values its copy of this schema names (ADR-0019 decision 1), so a build that predates fragments refuses a version-2 document by its version. spactl writes 2 on a document's first fragment and never lowers it. A later shape gets a later number, never a changed meaning.

revision.description: The registry's monotonic version. It must be greater than the live one; a rollback is the old content under a new revision. 'Greater than the live one' compares two documents, so the validator of task 2.1 checks it, not this schema.

apps.description: Every app in the cell. uniqueItems rejects two byte-identical entries. appId, host and oauth.clientId uniqueness is cross-entry, and a fragment's oauth.clientId is unique across every entry and every fragment, so the validator of task 2.1 checks them. An empty array is a valid document; deployment refuses to start a gateway against one (task 1.7).

if.$comment: ADR-0019 decision 2: a document whose entries carry any fragments is a later shape, so it declares schemaVersion 2. A document with none may declare 1 or 2.

appEntry.title: Registry entry
appEntry.description: One app. 'apis', 'csp' and 'fragments' may be absent: an app with no upstream, an app that adds nothing to the baseline content security policy, and an app that composes no fragments, which means what an entry meant before fragments existed. 'session' is required because the plan fixes no default lifetime.

appId.title: appId
appId.description: 3 to 40 lowercase letters, digits or hyphens. Unique in the registry; uniqueness is the validator's, not this schema's. It names the app's scheme pair, its S3 prefix and its log field.

host.title: host
host.description: The exact authority the browser sends, lowercase, with the port when one is used. Uppercase, a scheme, a path, userinfo or a trailing dot are rejected here. Two rules are not: the host is unique across entries, and it must end with a suffix Policy:AllowedHostSuffixes allows. Both are the validator's. The numeric port range is bounded loosely here (1 to 99999); the validator bounds it to 65535.

release.title: release
release.description: 1 to 64 letters, digits, dots, hyphens or underscores. It names the live S3 prefix: apps/{appId}/releases/{release}/ for an app, apps/{appId}/fragments/{fragmentId}/releases/{release}/ for a fragment. spactl checks that the prefix exists, and for a fragment that its entry file does; the gateway does not.

x-freeze.note: The oauth section is an identity part assigned to G1b. Task I-6 records the G0 report in ADR-0017; the annotated contracts-v1 tag records the freeze.

issuer.title: oauth.issuer
issuer.description: Names an issuer in platform configuration, under Issuers:{name}. That the name exists there is the validator's check, because this schema cannot see platform configuration. Which IIdpProfile applies is set beside the issuer, never in an entry.

clientId.title: oauth.clientId
clientId.description: The OAuth client id, unique across apps. Uniqueness is the validator's. Printable ASCII with no spaces.

clientSecretRef.title: oauth.clientSecretRef
clientSecretRef.description: A Parameter Store parameter and a version, as ssm:{name}:{version} (ADR-0003). Never a secret value: a credential never enters the registry. That the parameter can be read is resolved before a snapshot goes live, not here.

scopes.title: oauth.scopes
scopes.description: The scopes the app requests. 'openid' must be among them.

resource.title: oauth.resource
resource.description: Optional. When present it is one https URL, so the provider binds the access token's aud to the API's identifier. One audience per app in Phase 1.

apis.title: apis
apis.description: The upstreams the app reaches under /api/{name}/, or a fragment reaches under /fragments/{fragmentId}/api/{name}/. More than one upstream origin on one token set (the shell's apis, or one fragment's) is a warning, not an error: Phase 1 sends one access token to each, which is safe only inside one trust domain. A warning is not expressible here; the validator raises it.

name.description: The {name} segment in /api/{name}/, or in /fragments/{fragmentId}/api/{name}/. 1 to 32 lowercase letters, digits or hyphens, unique within the app or the fragment that lists it: the shell's names and each fragment's are separate namespaces. Uniqueness is the validator's.

upstream.description: One origin: scheme and authority only, with no path, query, fragment or credentials. It must also match Policy:AllowedUpstreams, which this schema cannot see, so the validator checks it. Phase 2 uses https patterns only.

timeoutSeconds.description: The entry's upstream idle timeout: the longest the upstream may stay silent, restarted on headers and on every body byte. Silence before the response headers is 504 upstream_timeout; after the headers and before the first body byte it is 502 upstream_unavailable (finding T-C18); once a body byte has been forwarded the response has started, and the call ends without a problem body. The maximum is the measured YARP 2.3.0 ceiling, added at G2 under ADR-0015 and ADR-0019: larger values cannot be applied as written.

csp.title: csp
csp.description: Sources added to the baseline content security policy, per directive. Only the directives the baseline sets may be extended; the baseline is in contracts/http-contract.md. A directive listed with no sources adds nothing, so an empty array is rejected.

allOf.$comment: 'unsafe-eval' is rejected in every directive. The letter classes stand in for case-insensitive matching, which content security policy keywords need and ECMA-262 patterns cannot flag.
data: is rejected in script-src. It stays allowed elsewhere; the example entry uses it in img-src.

fragments.title: fragments
fragments.description: The fragments this entry's app composes as a shell, in the order the gateway lists their schemes and merges their content security policy additions. Absent means none; an empty array is rejected, so no document has to declare schemaVersion 2 to say nothing. fragmentId is unique within the entry (DuplicateFragmentId), and how many fragments a shell may have is a Policy: value; both are the validator's. The schema sets no maxItems: a provider's limit on clients is a profile fact, not this contract's.

fragment.title: Fragment
fragment.description: One owner's unit, mounted into this entry's shell, with its own OAuth client, release, APIs and content security policy additions. It has no host and no session: the shell's host serves it, and the shell's session.lifetimeMinutes governs the one session. 'apis', 'csp' and 'entry' may be absent.

oauth.description: The whole oauth section, by reference and never forked: issuer is required, and resource is the fragment's own. The validator refuses an issuer other than the shell's (FragmentIssuerMismatch) and a clientId any other entry or fragment uses (DuplicateClientId).

fragmentId.title: fragmentId
fragmentId.description: 3 to 40 lowercase letters, digits or hyphens: the appId rule, so neither id can contain ':' and a fragment's scheme name oidc:{appId}:{fragmentId} parses one way. Unique within its shell's entry; uniqueness is the validator's. It names the fragment's scheme, its S3 prefix, its path namespace /fragments/{fragmentId}/ and its log field.

entry.title: entry
entry.description: The fragment's entry module: one .js file name at the root of its release, constant across releases and not hashed, which the shell loads with import() from /fragments/{fragmentId}/{entry}. The pattern admits no '/', so the file is never under assets/ or api/; a build whose entry is nested or hashed adds a one-line re-export at the root. Absent means entry.js. A release is complete when this file exists, which spactl checks on every registry write.

fragmentCsp.title: Fragment csp
fragmentCsp.description: Sources a fragment adds to its shell's content security policy, per directive. Narrower than csp: only these five directives, so a fragment cannot widen default-src, frame-ancestors, base-uri, form-action or object-src for the host, and its script-src names no 'strict-dynamic', nonce or hash. Every addition still applies to the whole document: the gateway sends one policy per host, the baseline, then the shell's csp, then each fragment's in registry order. A directive listed with no sources adds nothing, so an empty array is rejected.

allOf.$comment: 'strict-dynamic' is rejected in a fragment's script-src.
A nonce source is rejected in a fragment's script-src.
A hash source is rejected in a fragment's script-src. The one import map's hash is the shell's, in the shell entry's csp.

lifetimeMinutes.description: The session lifetime, between 5 and 720 minutes. There is no sliding expiry.
